questions.q: Why does this lesson say flat master records on their own aren't enough?
options: Because the real question is usually how related records roll up together, not what one record contains
Because flat records can never be stored in a relational database
Because a flat record cannot hold a unique ID
Because hierarchies eliminate the need for master records entirely
questions.explain: People usually ask roll-up questions, like how all customers under a parent company look together — answering that reliably requires an explicit hierarchy rather than ad hoc logic each time.

questions.q: What distinguishes a fixed-level hierarchy from a recursive hierarchy?
options: A fixed-level hierarchy always has the same number of levels for every record; a recursive hierarchy has variable depth
A fixed-level hierarchy only applies to employees, never to products
A recursive hierarchy cannot be used for reporting roll-ups
There is no real difference between the two
questions.explain: Brand to category to product is always exactly four levels (fixed), while a corporate family tree can be two levels for one customer and six for another (recursive).

questions.q: How does this lesson describe modeling a recursive hierarchy?
options: Each record stores its own ID and its direct parent's ID, and software walks the chain of parent pointers to assemble the tree
By creating one separate database table for every possible level of depth
By storing the entire tree as a single text field with no structure
Recursive hierarchies cannot be modeled in a table at all
questions.explain: A self-referencing parent-child structure lets a hierarchy of any depth be represented with one simple pattern, as shown in the lesson's example table.

questions.q: What does 'parent_id IS NULL' typically indicate in a recursive hierarchy table, per this lesson's example?
options: That the record is the ultimate parent at the top of the hierarchy
That the record has been deleted from the system
That the record is a duplicate awaiting review
That the record belongs to a different hierarchy entirely
questions.explain: A record with no parent_id has no row above it in the chain, which marks it as the top of that hierarchy — the ultimate parent.

questions.q: Why does this lesson say hierarchy maintenance belongs inside ongoing master data governance rather than being a one-time modeling exercise?
options: Because mergers, reorganizations, and reclassifications constantly change hierarchies after the initial build
Because hierarchies never actually change once correctly modeled
Because governance only applies to flat records, not hierarchical ones
Because recursive hierarchies automatically update themselves without any approval process
questions.explain: A hierarchy correct on launch day quietly becomes wrong the first time the business reorganizes, which is why each hierarchy change needs the same approval and effective-dating discipline as any other master data change.
